cards.text: Israel just walked across the Jordan on dry ground, and the kings of the land are melting with fear. Now, at that time, the LORD speaks to Joshua, Israel's leader. He tells him to make knives and circumcise the sons of Israel once again.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua what the knives should be made of. He says: make ___ knives.
Joshua does what the LORD says. He makes the knives and circumcises the sons of Israel.

cards.text: Now the passage stops to explain why. All the men of war who came out of Egypt had died on the journey through the wilderness.

cards.question: The men who came out of Egypt had all been circumcised. What about the sons born in the wilderness on the journey?

answers.text: None of them had been circumcised
Only the firstborn had been circumcised
Most had been circumcised on the way

cards.text: Israel wandered in the wilderness forty years, until all those men of war were gone. Forty YEARS. I spent a few years in a junk drawer and thought I was the world champion of waiting.

cards.question: Why did the men of war who came out of Egypt die in the wilderness?

answers.text: They did not obey the LORD
They were struck down by Egypt's army
They ran out of food on the journey

cards.question: Before they died, the LORD let those men of war see the land He had sworn to their fathers to give.

cards.text: So the LORD raised up their sons in their place. They're the ones Joshua circumcises, because nobody circumcised them along the way.

cards.question: After the whole nation has been circumcised, what does Israel do next?

answers.text: Stay in camp until they are healed
Cross back over the Jordan River

cards.text: Then the LORD says to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." Friend, I know a little something about having years of dust lifted off you in one moment.

cards.question: Because the LORD rolled away the reproach of Egypt, that place has been called ___ to this day.

cards.text: It's the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, and the Israelites are camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho. And this is no ordinary evening.

cards.question: On that evening at Gilgal, the Israelites keep the ___.
The day after the Passover, what do the Israelites eat?

answers.text: Unleavened bread and roasted grain from the land
Bread they had carried all the way from Egypt
Grain they had bought from the people of Jericho

cards.text: So now Israel has eaten from the produce of the land itself. And the very next day, something changes.

cards.question: The day after Israel eats from the produce of the land, what stops?
With no more manna, the Israelites have nothing to eat that year.

cards.text: If my oven quit on me after all those years, I'd stand there staring at it like it owed me money, but that year Israel eats the crops of the land of Canaan. Stick around, friend, because this story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: The card opens with facts from outside the passage: Israel crossing the Jordan on dry ground (Joshua 3:17) and the kings' hearts melting (Joshua 5:1). It cites only Joshua 5:2, so these facts have no reference.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card's verses field says Joshua 5:2, but the card also tells content from Joshua 5:1 (and 3:17). The citation doesn't match the verses the card tells.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke 'having years of dust lifted off you in one moment' calls back to the dust in the junk drawer. The line never says where the dust was, so the image doesn't click. It also reads as gentle and sentimental, not funny.

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'So now Israel has eaten from the produce of the land itself,' restates the answer to card 15 instead of moving the passage forward. Only the second sentence sets up the next moment.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The joke about his oven quitting and staring at it 'like it owed me money' is joined to the Bible fact with 'but.' This sets up a contrast with Israel that the text doesn't make and that doesn't click: it's unclear what Israel is being contrasted with. The joke and the fact run together in one long sentence.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
